ideas.motivation: The curvature forensics over 182 SID tables say the informative object is not a level's raw quotient-graph curvature (Spearman +0.03, p=0.65, confounded by level size) but the size-preserving-null-standardised curvature profile and specifically its across-level slope: standardised level-3 curvature correlates +0.26 with recall (+0.34 on mechanism families, p=0.001), level-1 curvature correlates -0.16, and their difference is -0.20 (p=0.0095), so SIDs whose prefix quotient curvature rises with depth recall better. Today that number is only a post-hoc predictor of finished SIDs. This idea turns the slope into a training-time design target: the RQ-VAE must produce a code partition whose standardised quotient curvature is non-decreasing in depth, and the only free variables that can satisfy that target are the per-level curvature values of the hyperbolic metric the quantizer assigns in. Level 1 is therefore pushed toward the expander-like end and level 3 toward the clustered end, which is the direction the data wants and is the opposite of the Issue #127 failure, where the coarse level was aligned to a 17-cell behavioural partition, collapsed to 4 codes and fell to 0.0513.
ideas.novelty: Three things are new relative to everything already tried here. (1) The curvature parameter of the space is not set by a formula from a behavioural score (the CURVCTRL-SID shape), not a per-item rank or radius (the BRad-RQ shape) and not a successor-weighted Frechet mean (the round-128 shape): each level's curvature is a trainable parameter whose gradient is supplied by a hinge on the standardised curvature of the partition the quantizer is actually producing, so curvature becomes an output of a matching problem, not an input knob. (2) The matching target is the null-standardised, group-size-controlled quantity, so the level-size confound that made the raw curvature useless is removed inside the loop; the null (10 membership shuffles with the code histogram held fixed) is re-estimated every 250 epochs from the current partition. (3) The target is a profile order (level 1 <= level 2 <= level 3), not a level-wise absolute value, so no level is pinned to a number and no constant has to be chosen; the hinge margin is 0, which is the sign boundary of the measured -0.20 effect, not a tuned value.
ideas.observables: eta_1, eta_2, eta_3 and c_l over training; the standardised profile (kappa-tilde_1, kappa-tilde_2, kappa-tilde_3) of the hard SID at each null re-estimate; the two hinge terms; the number of codes actually used per level and the collision rate; the existing prefix behaviour-predictability and adjacency diagnostics; Stage-3 test_recall@10. Expected: the hinge terms fall, eta_1 becomes negative and/or eta_3 positive (a rising profile), level-1 usage rises or holds, level-3 usage holds, and test_recall@10 rises above the baseline.

risks: (1) The differentiable curvature surrogate may be dominated by the temperature and the sampled edge set rather than by the partition, so eta_l drifts for reasons unrelated to behaviour and (a) passes while (c) fails. (2) The target is measured on the level-l code-marginal quotient (K nodes) rather than on the level-l prefix-tuple quotient used in the forensics (up to K^l nodes), because a per-step null over prefix tuples is outside the step budget; the marginal may have the opposite slope for some tables. (3) Hyperbolic arccosh gradients blow up when two codes coincide, which is exactly the collapse mode of #127; the radial squash, the tau floor and the usage guard are the only defences and they may not be enough. (4) At level 3 the partition is nearly pure, so the shuffle null can have a near-zero sigma and kappa-tilde explodes and hijacks the total loss; the sigma floor mitigates but also weakens the signal. (5) With one run and no ablation, a null result cannot distinguish "the slope target is wrong" from "the surrogate gradient is bad", and that ambiguity must be reported rather than resolved.
ideas.safeguards: arccosh argument clamped to [1 + 1e-6, 1e6] and the Lorentz inner product clamped before the arccosh; c_l floored at 1e-3 and eta clipped to [-2.3, 2.3]; tau_l floored at 1e-3; the W1 normaliser d_{L,c}(e_a,e_b) floored at 1e-6 and edges with B_l mass below 1e-6 of the maximum dropped, so coincident codes cannot produce an infinite curvature; Sinkhorn in the log domain with a 1e-8 shift and 3 fixed iterations so its cost is bounded and its gradient finite; residuals passed through the smooth radial squash u/(1 + ||u||/10) so no point reaches the hyperboloid boundary; sigma_l floored at 0.05|mu_l| + 1e-6 so a near-pure level-3 partition cannot make kappa-tilde explode; deterministic top-128 edge selection so the loss is reproducible without a seed sweep; a non-finite L_curv sets that step's curvature gradient to zero and increments a counter that is reported; the usage guard freezes eta_l whenever the level's used-code count falls below 0.9x its epoch-0 value, which is the explicit defence against the Issue #127 collapse to 4 codes; K is never reduced and no code is ever merged.
ideas.spec_equations:
pseudocode per step
inputs: batch X (1023 x d_x), W~_batch (1023 x 1023 sparse, 20 nnz/row), eta (3,), a (3 x 256 x d)
for l in 1..3:
    c[l] = 1.0 * exp(clip(eta[l], -2.3, 2.3))
    e[l] = expmap0(a[l], c[l])                      # 256 x (d+1)
    D[l] = lorentz_dist(e[l], e[l], c[l])           # 256 x 256, diag 0
residuals: u[1] = z; v[1] = squash(u[1]); k[1] = argmin_k D[1][v[1], k]
           u[l] = z - sum_{m<l} logmap0(e[m][k[m]], c[m]); v[l] = squash(u[l]); ...
P[l] = softmax_k( -dist(v[l], e[l], c[l]) / (1/sqrt(c[l])) )
B[l] = P[l]^T W~_batch P[l]; B[l] = 0.5 (B[l] + B[l]^T)
deg[l] = B[l] 1; m[a] = 0.5 onehot(a) + 0.5 B[l][a,:] / deg[l][a]
E[l] = top 128 edges of B[l] by mass
for (a,b) in E[l]:
    C = D[l][supp(a), supp(b)]                    # 8 x 8 ground cost
    pi = sinkhorn(m[a][supp(a)], m[b][supp(b)], C / (0.05 mean(D[l])), iters=3)
    W1 = sum(pi * C); kappa[a,b] = 1 - W1 / max(D[l][a,b], 1e-6)
khat[l] = sum_E B[l] * kappa / sum_E B[l]
ktilde[l] = (khat[l] - mu[l]) / max(sigma[l], 0.05 abs(mu[l]) + 1e-6)
Lcurv = max(0, ktilde[1] - ktilde[2])^2 + max(0, ktilde[2] - ktilde[3])^2
L = L_RQ + lambda * Lcurv
mu, sigma refreshed every 250 epochs: for r in 1..10 permute the item->code map preserving code sizes, recompute khat with the same e[l] and the same edge rule; mu[l] = mean_r, sigma[l] = std_r
usage guard: if usedcodes[l] < 0.9 * usedcodes[l](epoch 0) then zero the gradient of eta[l] for the next 100 epochs
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the batch of encoder outputs z (1023 x d), the training-graph block W~_batch, the tangent codebooks a (3 x 256 x d), the trainable curvatures eta (3,), and the cached null statistics mu, sigma (3,). Outputs are the per-level curvatures c_l, the soft posteriors P_l (1023 x 256) that also define the hard SID, the scalar L_curv and its gradient dL_curv/deta_l (3,), the updated null statistics on the 250-epoch boundary, and the logged curvature profile and usage counts.

specification.text: Frozen protocol objects unchanged: encoder f_phi, L = 3 residual levels, codebook size K per level (K = 256 used for all arithmetic below), Euclidean reconstruction, straight-through assignment, 3000 Stage-2 epochs, 24 steps/epoch, batch floor(24556/24) = 1023 items. Behaviour graph from the training split only: W[i,j] = n(i->j) + n(j->i) over consecutive pairs of training sequences, degree-normalised W~[i,j] = W[i,j]/sqrt(d_i d_j), d_i = sum_j W[i,j], sparsified to the 20 largest entries per row. Per-level curvature eta_l in R trainable with eta_l(0) = 0, c_l = c_0 exp(eta_l), documented default c_0 = 1.0, eta_l clipped to [-2.3, +2.3]. Tangent codebook a_{l,k} in R^d, atom e_{l,k} = exp_0^{c_l}(a_{l,k}); encoder residual u_i^(l) = z_i - sum_{m<l} log_0^{c_m}(e_{m,k_m}); the point quantised is v_i^(l) = u_i^(l)/(1 + ||u_i^(l)||/r_max) with numeric guard r_max = 10. Selection k_l = argmin_k d_{L,c_l}(v_i^(l), e_{l,k}); the frozen Euclidean commitment is replaced one-for-one by d^2_{L,c_l}(v_i^(l), e_{l,k}) with no new coefficient; the decoder keeps consuming the tangent vectors sum_l a_{l,k_l}, so the generative Stage-3 interface is untouched. Behaviour-curvature target inside the step: p_l(i,k) = softmax_k(-d_{L,c_l}(v_i^(l), e_{l,k})/tau_l), tau_l = 1/sqrt(c_l); B_l = P_l^T W~_batch P_l symmetrised; lazy walk m_a = 0.5 e_a + 0.5 B_l[a,:]/sum(B_l[a,:]); kappa_l(a,b) = 1 - W1(m_a, m_b)/d_{L,c_l}(e_{l,a}, e_{l,b}) with W1 an entropic Sinkhorn (3 iterations, eps = 0.05 * mean_{a,b} d_{L,c_l}, a measured scale) on the 8x8 support; kappa-hat_l = mass-weighted mean over the top-128 edges of B_l by mass; standardise kappa-tilde_l = (kappa-hat_l - mu_l)/max(sigma_l, 0.05|mu_l| + 1e-6) where mu_l, sigma_l come from R = 10 shuffles of the item->code map preserving the code histogram, recomputed every 250 epochs from the current hard partition; L_curv = max(0, kappa-tilde_1 - kappa-tilde_2)^2 + max(0, kappa-tilde_2 - kappa-tilde_3)^2; L = L_RQ + lambda * L_curv with lambda = L_RQ(step 0)/max(L_curv(step 0), 1e-6) measured once at initialisation.

ideas.title: A size-preserving null-calibrated curvature hinge on the per-level code quotient learns the per-level curvature of a hyperbolic RQ-VAE quantizer

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: delta_l = 0 for all levels, i.e. W is not read, c_l = c0 and rho_l = rho0; everything else identical (still Lorentzian, unit curvature, median radius).
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full loop above, kappa_hat measured from the training quotient graph and spent on both c_l and rho_l. Only this arm is trained this round; the other two exist behind switches, are correct, and are not run.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_l replaced by the flat limit c -> 0 (Euclidean squared distance, no arcosh, no exp/log) while delta_l and rho_l keep their behaviour-driven values, i.e. a Euclidean quantizer with behaviour-set radius.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: for every consecutive pair (i -> j) in a training session inside window H, increment W_ij; symmetrise. At each refresh multiply W by the current item->prefix indicator per level to get A_l, then build the lazy random walk and the per-edge Ollivier curvature with a Sinkhorn-W1 over each sampled edge's neighbour support. No validation or test interaction, user or item is read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Sequential co-consumption / directed item transitions of the training split, aggregated to prefix-group level as a weighted quotient graph, plus the current model's training-item prefix assignment.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step the extra work is three Lorentz distance tensors of shape B x K x (D+1) plus three exp/log maps of shape B x D per item and per code: about 1.2e6 extra flops at B=256, K=256, D=64, under 2% of a step, with no backward pass through the measurement. The 15 curvature refreshes cost one sparse S_l^T W S_l per level (3 x nnz(W) ~ 3e6 adds), 8 null relabellings, and 3 levels x 256 sampled edges x 30 Sinkhorn iterations on supports of at most 9+9 cells (~1.5e7 flops per refresh, a few seconds each), so roughly 30-60 s of the whole 72000-step run: under 1% wall clock and no extra memory beyond one 24556 x 3 assignment cache.
ideas.coupling_equation: p_l(k|i) = softmax_k( -d_{L,c_l}( exp_o^{c_l}( rho_l*tanh(||r_{l,i}||/rho_l)*rhat_{l,i} ), exp_o^{c_l}( rho_l*tanh(||w_{l,k}||/rho_l)*what_{l,k} ) ) ), with c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l), rho_l = rho0*exp(delta_l/2), delta_l = clip(kappa_hat_l - mean_m kappa_hat_m, -1, +1), kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l(A_l(W_train, p_l)) - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, and rho0 = median_i ||z_i - mean(z)|| measured on training items at epoch 0.
ideas.coupling_path: training behaviour graph W -> quotient graph Q_l of the current prefixes -> standardised curvature kappa_hat_l -> delta_l -> (c_l, rho_l) -> Lorentz distance d_{L,c_l}(exp_o^{c_l}(squash(r_{l,i})), e_{l,k}) -> argmin / straight-through -> new prefixes -> next refresh of Q_l. Behaviour off collapses kappa_hat to 0 and forces every level to unit curvature and the median radius; geometry off (c_l -> 0 with rho_l kept) leaves a Euclidean quantizer with the same behaviour-set radius. Both change the argmin, hence the SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If level-wise clustering of the training behaviour graph is a real constraint on a good prefix code, then letting the more clustered sub-quotient (typically level 3) own a flatter, wider hyperboloid while the more branching level (typically level 1) owns a sharper, tighter one must (a) keep level-3 code usage at or above baseline, (b) not collapse level-1 usage, (c) make the run's measured standardised profile monotone in depth, and (d) push Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. Observed from the run's own logs: per-level used-code counts, the 15 recorded kappa_hat triples, and test_recall@10 against 0.065; if the profile is not monotone or level-1 usage falls below about 8 codes the hypothesis is falsified.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer: codebook parameterisation (each code is exp_o^{c_l} of a radius-squashed free tangent vector), encoder-side residual mapping exp_o^{c_l}, the nearest-code rule argmin d_{L,c_l}, and residual subtraction in the tangent space log_o^{c_l}. It therefore acts on the assignment and on every gradient reaching encoder and codebooks.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Measured (not tuned) negative curvature per level, c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l) with c0 = 1, realised in the Lorentz hyperboloid model of curvature -c_l: d_{L,c}(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c))*arcosh(-c*<x,y>_L), exp_o^c(v) = (cosh(sqrt(c)||v||)/sqrt(c), sinh(sqrt(c)||v||)/(sqrt(c)||v||)*v), log_o^c its inverse, Euclidean branch as the c->0 limit.
ideas.key_change: Each RQ level l lives on its own Lorentz hyperboloid of curvature -c_l with code radius rho_l, both set from that level's standardised behaviour-quotient curvature, c_l = c0*exp(-delta_l) and rho_l = rho0*exp(delta_l/2) with delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l(kappa_hat_l). Nearest-code assignment, residual subtraction and codebook parameterisation all pass through the exp/log maps of that level's hyperboloid, so changing delta_l changes which code each item receives.
ideas.leakage_boundary: W, the quotient graphs, the null draws and sigma are computed exclusively from training-split sessions of the frozen Stage-2 split; validation and test interactions are never read while the SID is constructed, and the mechanism has no validation-based selection, no early stopping and no test-time statistic. The 0.065 target and the forensic correlations fix the mechanism's direction before the run only; no recall label of any model enters kappa_hat.
ideas.motivation: The measured evidence says the recall-relevant geometric object is the level-wise profile of the behaviour quotient graph's standardised Ollivier curvature (L3 +0.26, L1 -0.16, L1-L3 -0.20, p=0.0095), and that the largest non-geometric driver is how many level-3 codes actually get used (+0.42, collisions -0.39). Existing SIDs differ only in whether their prefix geometry happens to fit the level-wise clustering of the behaviour graph. No quantizer currently builds that fit: the partition comes from one Euclidean nearest-code rule with a single curvature shared by all three levels.
ideas.novelty: Not a per-level learning rate from a hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), not entropy-ranked radial assignment (BRad-RQ), not Frechet codebook updates, and not a fixed mixed-curvature product chosen by hand. The signal is a runtime-measured, permutation-null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the behaviour quotient graph induced by the CURRENT prefix assignment, spent as a mean-zero allocation of two geometric quantities (per-level negative curvature c_l and per-level radial budget rho_l) that enter the distance the quantizer itself minimises. No extra loss term is added, no recall label is used, and the assignment feeds back into the measurement, so behaviour and geometry form a closed loop rather than two parallel objectives.
ideas.observables: per-level used-code counts over training (level 3 expected at or above baseline, level 1 expected not to collapse); the 15 logged kappa_hat triples and their depth profile; the final SID table's collision rate; the recorded behaviour-prefix transfer predictability (diagnostic only, never a gate); final Stage3 test_recall@10 against 0.065.
risks: The sign of the curvature-to-geometry map may be wrong for this data (flatter may need to follow LOW curvature), and one run cannot correct it; the +-1 clip keeps the worst case a bounded factor-e perturbation of one level instead of a collapse. The assignment<->curvature loop can oscillate, damped by the T=200 cadence, EMA 0.5 and the mean-zero constraint. Sinkhorn W1 on sparse quotient graphs is noisy and biased upward; the identical estimator is applied to the null so standardisation cancels the bias but amplifies variance when sigma_null is small, hence the sigma floor. The tangent-space residual chain is less faithful than the Euclidean one and can degrade reconstruction; the measured radial normalisation makes the tanh squash near-identity for typical items.
ideas.safeguards: arcosh argument clamped to >= 1+1e-7, evaluated in float32 after subtracting the time component, with the c <= 1e-4 branch replaced by the Euclidean formula; every code and residual squashed by rho_l*tanh(.) so sqrt(c_l)||v|| <= sqrt(c_l)*rho_l stays O(1) and exp_o cannot overflow; delta clipped to +-1 (one standardised sigma maps to a factor e) and EMA-smoothed 0.5 so a noisy null cannot jump the geometry; kappa_hat set to 0 whenever a level has fewer than 8 occupied prefixes or sigma_null < 1e-6, which falls back to unit curvature (also the behaviour-off arm); mean-zero constraint on delta so the total curvature budget is conserved and code usage cannot be globally inflated or deflated; rho0 measured from training items so the squash is near-identity for typical residuals; the standard usage/entropy term and the codebook size are untouched, so nothing forces prefix merging and the Issue #127 coarse-partition collapse cannot be reproduced by construction.
ideas.spec_equations:
# once, from the training split only
  W = sym(cooccurrence(train_sessions, window=H)); N = 24556
  rho0 = median_i ||z_i - mean(z)||          # measured at epoch 0
  c0 = 1.0; delta = zeros(3)
  for epoch in 1..3000:
      for step in 1..24:
          for l in 1..3:
              c_l = c0*exp(-delta[l]); rho_l = rho0*exp(delta[l]/2)
              x   = exp_o(c_l, rho_l*tanh(||r_l||/rho_l)*rhat_l)          # item side
              E   = exp_o(c_l, rho_l*tanh(||w_l||/rho_l)*what_l)          # codes, free tangents w_l
              logits = -d_L(c_l, x[:,None,:], E[None,:,:])
              k_l = argmin(logits, -1)                                    # straight-through
              u_l = log_o(c_l, E[k_l])                                    # tangent code
              r_{l+1} = r_l - u_l
          z_hat = LayerNorm(sum_l u_l); loss = recon + commit + baseline usage term
          adam_step(encoder, {w_l})                                       # c_l, rho_l stop-grad
      if epoch % 200 == 0:
          for l in 1..3:
              A_l = S_l(p_l)^T @ W @ S_l(p_l)                              # quotient graph
              d_Q = hopdist(A_l); P = 0.5*(I + D^{-1}A_l)
              kappa_bar_l = mean over 256 weight-sampled edges of (1 - sinkhornW1(m_a,m_b,d_Q)/d_Q(a,b))
              for r in 1..8:
                  p_l^null = shuffle_members(p_l)                          # group sizes preserved
                  recompute kappa_bar_l^null identically
              mu, sigma = mean/std(kappa_bar_l^null)
              kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l - mu)/max(sigma, 1e-6)
          delta = 0.5*delta + 0.5*clip(kappa_hat - mean(kappa_hat), -1, +1)
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-split co-occurrence W, item representations z_i and residuals r_{l,i}, current hard prefixes, free codebook tangents w_{l,k}, measured rho0. Outputs: per-level (c_l, rho_l) refreshed every 200 epochs, per-item codes k_1..k_3 (the SID), the tangent code vectors u_l for the decoder, and the reconstruction consumed by the standard RQ-VAE loss.

specification.text: (1) Build W once from the training split: W_ij = number of training sessions in which j occurs after i within the same window H used by the sequential Stage-2 encoder, symmetrised W <- (W+W^T)/2; N_tr = 24556. (2) Every T = 200 epochs (15 refreshes over 3000 epochs) take the current hard prefixes p_l(i) = (k_1..k_l) and form the quotient graph Q_l: nodes = occupied level-l prefixes, A_l(a,b) = sum_{i in a, j in b} W_ij (sparse S_l^T W S_l, self-loops kept); d_Q = unweighted hop distance. (3) Lazy walk P = 0.5(I + D^{-1}A) with D = diag(A1); curvature kappa(a,b) = 1 - W1(m_a, m_b)/d_Q(a,b) with m_a = 0.5*delta_a + 0.5*A_a./deg(a). (4) Standardise against a member-shuffling null: R = 8 relabellings of items into prefixes with group sizes preserved, kappa_hat_l = (kappa_bar_l - mu_null,l)/sigma_null,l, the same edge sample size used in both. (5) Form delta_l with the mean-zero constraint, clip to [-1,+1], EMA with 0.5. (6) All distances, residuals and codebooks use the level's own hyperboloid. STOP-GRADIENT on kappa_hat: it is a schedule, not a loss.

ideas.title: Mean-zero allocation of per-level Lorentz curvature and code radius from the null-standardised Ollivier curvature of the training behaviour quotient graph

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Same code path, flag use_behaviour_curvature=False: Phi set to 0 for every level and code, so k_{l,c}=k0 everywhere and the curved quantizer runs with a single uniform curvature. Nothing else changes.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Full path above, one training run, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Flag use_curvature_metric=False: the field is still computed and logged but the assignment uses the Euclidean squared distance ||z-e||^2 and the curvature never enters the logits.
ideas.behavior_computation: From each training sequence, consecutive pairs (i_t -> i_{t+1}); W_ij counts them, W <- W+W^T. At a refresh, the 4096-item fixed sample's induced subgraph is contracted by the current hard level-l assignment a_l to give w_ab; degrees, lazy walk, W1 transport on neighbour supports, node curvature, then the 20-shuffle size-preserving null. Reference mu*_l, sd*_l come from the same estimator applied to P*_l built from W.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions (sequential co-consumption) in the training split, aggregated into the level's prefix quotient graph.
ideas.cost_estimate: 72,000 optimizer steps (3000x24), batch 1023. Per-step assignment over 3x256x64 is ~50M mul-adds; the Mobius/artanh path adds ~10 elementwise passes over 0.8M values, under 1 ms/step and under 1% of a model step. Six hundred refreshes (every 5 epochs) cost one 4096-item forward (4 step-equivalents, 2400 step-equivalents total = 3.3%) plus 20 null shuffles x 3 levels x ~5k edges x 4 Sinkhorn iterations, roughly 0.1-1 s each, 1-10 min total. One-off reference SVD+k-means under 15 min. Expected +4-8% wall clock, no extra forward/backward in the 72k steps.
ideas.coupling_equation: p(c|i,l) ∝ exp( -(2/sqrt(k_{l,c})) artanh(sqrt(k_{l,c}) ||(-z_{i,l}) (+)_{k_{l,c}} e_{l,c}||) / tau_l ), with k_{l,c}=clip(k0*exp(-(kappa_hat^{ORC}_{l,c}(W_train,a_l)-mu*_l)/sd*_l), k0/4, 4k0).
ideas.coupling_path: W_train -> level-l quotient Q(a_l) -> standardised node curvature kappa_hat_{l,c} -> deviation from the K_l-cell behaviour reference -> per-code chart curvature k_{l,c} -> the distance used to assign every residual at that level -> new a_l and new codebook gradients -> next refresh. Behaviour sets the curvature, the curvature is the metric, the metric sets the assignment; neither can be removed without changing the same tensor that the loss differentiates.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If per-cell geometry matched to the cell's own quotient curvature is what the generative prefixes need, the produced SID should use more level-3 codes and collide less at fixed K, its standardised curvature profile should move toward the resolution-matched reference profile, and Stage3 test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065 in the single run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE nearest-code rule at each of the three levels, i.e., in the E-step of quantization and in the gradient that reaches the encoder and the codebook through the assignment probabilities.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance with per-code curvature magnitude k_{l,c} (curvature -k_{l,c}), d_k(x,y)=(2/sqrt(k)) artanh(sqrt(k)||(-x) (+)k y||), with Mobius addition (+)k; k0 is data-derived and the field lives in [k0/4, 4k0].
ideas.key_change: The RQ-VAE distance at level l becomes d_{k_{l,c}}(z,e_c) with a per-code curvature magnitude k_{l,c} obtained from the code's standardised quotient curvature; the field is refreshed every 5 epochs from training transitions and enters the assignment logits directly, so both the partition and the codebook gradients move.
ideas.leakage_boundary: W is built only from training-split sequences; the reference SVD/k-means, k0 (from training residual norms) and every refresh use only training items and the current model. No validation or test item, sequence, co-occurrence or metric is read at any point; the SID table is frozen before Stage 3 and Stage 3 never writes back.
ideas.motivation: The SID's prefix geometry is fixed and Euclidean for every codeword, so a codeword sitting on a tree-like (branching) behavioural neighbourhood and one sitting inside a cohesive cluster are forced to discriminate residuals identically. The forensics show the standardised level profile, not the raw curvature, is what tracks recall, and that level-3 code usage and collisions dominate. What is missing is a mechanism that gives each codeword a geometry matched to its own behavioural quotient neighbourhood, at the level's own resolution, without ever coarsening the partition.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds set a per-LEVEL curvature from a scalar (hard prefix-transition score) or a per-code radius from context entropy. This sets a per-CODE curvature MAGNITUDE from the standardised Ollivier-Ricci curvature of that code's node in the level's behaviour quotient, expressed as a deviation from a resolution-matched behaviour reference partition (exactly K_l cells), and makes that number the curvature of that code's Poincare chart inside the nearest-code rule. The curvature is not a loss, a schedule or a radius: it is the metric in which the residual-to-codeword distance is measured, per code, per level.
ideas.observables: Per-level code usage histogram and dead-code count (level 3 should rise); SID triple collision rate (should fall); the produced SID's standardised curvature profile per level versus the reference profile (should move toward it, i.e., flatten where the reference is flat); conditional entropy H(prefix_{l+1}|prefix_l) on held-out training sequences (recorded, not gating); Stage3 test_recall@10.
risks: Per-pair curvature is not a global metric, so cells need not be convex and a code can become over-attractive; node curvature on small cells is noisy and can flip sign between refreshes; if the reference partition is itself strongly aligned with W, Phi may saturate the +-3 clip and the field becomes binary; added curvature could interact badly with the straight-through gradient at level 1 and shrink early code usage, which is exactly the Issue #127 failure mode.
ideas.safeguards: clamp sqrt(k)||x|| to 1-1e-6 before artanh and clamp squared norms to (1-1e-3)^2/k; keep k in [k0/4,4k0] so no code can approach the ball boundary; winsorise Phi at +-3; shrink Phi by n_c/(n_c+nbar_l) so small cells cannot dominate; EMA 0.9 on the field and refresh only every 5 epochs to damp the assignment-curvature loop; dead-code revival at k0/4 guarantees at least half the codebook is reachable, so the Issue #127 collapse to a handful of level-1 codes is structurally blocked and K_l is never reduced; if a refresh finds the assignment entropy below ln(K_l/2) the field update is skipped for that level; all curvature arithmetic in float64 on the graph side.

If usage_c<1/(2K_l) then k_{l,c}=k0/4 until the next refresh. specification.text: (1) Build W (24556x24556, symmetrised directed transition counts) from training sequences only. ideas.title: Behaviour-curvature cell charts: per-code standardised Ollivier curvature sets each RQ codeword's own Poincare chart curvature used in assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: z_l set to 0 for all levels, so z*_l=0 and c_l=1; the hyperbolic machinery stays exactly as specified (unit curvature ball), the graph and null are still computed and logged, but no behaviour quantity enters the geometry.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run, c_l from z*_l, curved log/transport/exp/distance active; this is the single trained candidate.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_l=1 and every curved operation replaced by its flat limit, log_p(x)=x-p, exp=addition, transport=identity, distance=Euclidean, while the behaviour term survives only as the per-level residual scale exp(z*_l/2) multiplying (x-p), so the behaviour switch remains live in the Euclidean arm.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: consecutive item pairs in each training sequence give directed counts; prefixes come from the current SID table (which itself is built only on training items); for each level l contract items into prefix groups, build the undirected weighted quotient with within-group mass kept as self-loops, build the 1/2-lazy walk, compute W1 by entropic optimal transport on the neighbour support using shortest-path distances inside Q_l, average kappa by edge mass, and standardise against 16 label shuffles that preserve group sizes; all of this is a function of the training graph and the training-time partition only.
ideas.behavior_signal: Edge-mass-weighted mean Ollivier curvature of the lazy random walk on the training-transition quotient graph induced by each prefix level, standardised against a group-size-preserving member-shuffle null; the resulting three-level profile is converted into the depth-monotone target z*_l.
ideas.cost_estimate: Baseline frozen scale is 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps. Per step the added work is, for batch 1024 and d=64, two Möbius additions, one artanh, one normalisation and one exp map, about 0.5-1 MFLOP, i.e. roughly +5 to +10 percent of a step; codebook and model size unchanged. Curvature is recomputed 61 times (epoch 1, every 50 epochs, final): each recomputation is one bincount pass over the transition edge list (order 10^6 ints, tens of milliseconds) plus entropic W1 on at most 50000 quotient edges with support capped at 64 neighbours, about 1-3 s. Total curvature overhead about 2-4 minutes, under 5 percent of the 3000-epoch wall clock; memory +O(E) ints and 3 scalars.
ideas.coupling_equation: r_l = (lambda^{c_l}_{p_{l-1}} / 2) * log^{c_l}_{p_{l-1}}(x), with c_l = exp(-clip(zbar + (l-2) min(1, |z_1-z_3|/2), -2, 2)) and lambda^{c}_{p}=2/(1-c||p||^2); the behaviour term is z_l inside c_l, the curved term is the Möbius logarithm.
ideas.coupling_path: transition graph -> quotient Q_l -> kbar_l -> z_l -> target z*_l -> c_l -> Möbius log at p_{l-1} -> residual direction -> nearest code k_l -> next prefix point -> next level's residual. Behaviour and curvature meet in the same operator (the log map's Möbius term), so removing behaviour fixes c_l=1 and changes the residual direction, and removing curvature replaces the log map by subtraction and changes the residual direction too.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the signed curvature profile is causal rather than a correlate of code usage, then imposing z_3 > z_1 through the ball curvature should make level-3 cells behaviourally tighter while level 1 stays branchy, and should show up as (a) unchanged or larger level-3 used-code count, (b) z_3 - z_1 > 0 measured on the final SID, (c) Stage3 test recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer's forward pass and its straight-through gradient path, at every level l in {1,2,3}: the encoder point is exp-mapped with c_l, the residual is the Möbius log at the accumulated prefix point, and the prefix step is an exp map; the reconstruction term is a geodesic distance.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with trainable-free, behaviour-derived negative curvature magnitude c_l = exp(-z*_l), clipped to [e^-2, e^2]: Möbius addition, exponential and logarithmic maps, parallel transport to the origin with conformal factor lambda_p, and geodesic distance d_c.
ideas.key_change: For each prefix level, the training-transition quotient graph's standardised Ollivier curvature is turned into a depth-monotone target profile and then into a per-level curvature magnitude c_l; the RQ residual is the curvature-c_l Möbius logarithm of the item point at its accumulated prefix point, so c_l rotates and rescales the residual before nearest-code selection.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition graph is built once from training sequences before any SID training, and the quotient is a contraction of that frozen graph by the current training-time code assignment; no validation or test sequence, no validation/test co-occurrence, and no held-out recall enters the curvature, the target, the clip bounds or the guard thresholds. Validation and test items are never used to set c_l, and the only test quantity read is the final Stage3 test_recall@10.
ideas.motivation: The forensic evidence says the recall is not explained by the raw curvature of the behaviour quotient graph but by its standardised profile: level-3 curvature is positively associated with recall (+0.34 over mechanism families), level-1 negatively (-0.16), and the difference L1 minus L3 is negative (-0.20, p=0.0095). Existing SID quantizers cannot act on that, because the partition's curvature is only ever measured after the fact, and because the strongest non-geometric predictor, level-3 code usage (+0.42), collapses when a quantizer is forced toward a coarser behavioural partition (Issue #127: level 1 fell to 4 codes, recall 0.0513). We need a quantizer whose geometry is driven by the measured curvature profile while keeping item-level resolution.
ideas.novelty: Earlier arms here changed codebook positions (successor-weighted Frechet), changed radial placement by behaviour entropy, or ran a per-level curvature controller on hard transition scores. This idea does none of those: code positions, codebook size, radii and entropy are untouched. The behaviour curvature sets only the negative curvature c_l of the Poincare ball in which the Möbius log map is taken at the current prefix point, so curvature changes the direction of the residual and therefore which code the next level sees. Removing the behaviour term or replacing the ball by its flat limit changes the code choice at levels 2 and 3, not just a loss value.
ideas.observables: per-level code occupancy and its perplexity, prefix collision rate, the measured standardised profile z_1,z_2,z_3 of the final SID's quotient graphs, per-level gradient norms of the codebook and encoder, and Stage3 test_recall@10.
risks: The association may be confounded by level-3 code usage, so the mechanism could raise z_3 while recall stays flat; the target could overshoot and saturate distances so that few codes win, which the occupancy guard only catches after the fact; the recomputation lag of 50 epochs may make c_l stale as the partition moves; in the nearly flat regime the transport may be near-identity and the effect may be small; the profile target is derived from a null that is itself noisy at level 3 where many groups are singletons.
ideas.safeguards: clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-7 and ||p|| to (1-1e-6)/sqrt(c) before every log/exp; assert c in [e^-2,e^2] and skip the update on NaN/Inf keeping the previous c_l; cap W1 support at the top 64 neighbours per node and cap sampled quotient edges at 50000 by edge weight, renorma-lising the walk; occupancy guard reverts c_1 if fewer than K/2 level-1 codes (K = codebook size, about 256, i.e. 128 codes) hold at least 1 percent of training items, and reverts c_3 if level-3 used codes fall below half of their epoch-1 value; no item is merged or reassigned to a coarser partition, so Issue #127-style resolution loss cannot come from the mechanism itself; the curvature null uses a fixed 16 draws and a fixed seed so the target is reproducible within the single run.
ideas.spec_equations: (1) Q_l: nodes are distinct length-l prefixes; w_l(p,q)=W_l(p,q)+W_l(q,l p) with W_l(p,q)=#{(u->v) in T : pref_l(u)=p, pref_l(v)=q}; s_l(p)=#{(u->v): pref_l(u)=pref_l(v)=p}; d_l(p)=sum_q w_l(p,q)+2 s_l(p). (2) lazy walk m_p = 0.5*delta_p + 0.5*sum_q (w_l(p,q)/sum_q w_l(p,q)) delta_q. (3) Ollivier kappa_l(p,q)=1 - W1(m_p,m_q)/dist_{Q_l}(p,q). (4) kbar_l = sum_{p<q} w_l(p,q) kappa_l(p,q) / sum_{p<q} w_l(p,q). (5) null: 16 shuffles of the item->prefix label vector preserving group sizes, same computation, giving mu_l, sigma_l; z_l=(kbar_l-mu_l)/max(sigma_l,1e-6). (6) zbar=(z_1+z_2+z_3)/3; m=min(1, |z_1-z_3|/2); z*_l=clip(zbar+(l-2)*m, -2, 2); c_l=exp(-z*_l). (7) ball B_c={x: c||x||^2<1}, lambda_x=2/(1-c||x||^2), a(+)b=((1+2c<a,b>+c||b||^2)a+(1-c||a||^2)b)/(1+2c<a,b>+c^2||a||^2||b||^2). (8) exp_0(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v/(sqrt(c)||v||). (9) log_p(x)= (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-p)(+)x||) * ((-p)(+)x)/||(-p)(+)x||. (10) transport to origin PT_{p->0}(v)=(lambda_p/2) v. (11) r_l=(lambda_{p_{l-1}}/2) log^{c_l}_{p_{l-1}}(x), with x=exp^{c_l}_0(h). (12) k_l=argmin_k ||r_l-e_{l,k}||. (13) p_l=exp^{c_l}_{p_{l-1}}((2/lambda_{p_{l-1}}) e_{l,k_l}); p_0=0. (14) L = sum_l d_{c_l}(x, p_l)^2 + ||sg(r_l)-e_{l,k_l}||^2 + 0.25 ||r_l-sg(e_{l,k_l})||^2, d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||). (15) flavour: canonical prefix point maintained in B_1 and mapped into B_{c_l} by x -> sqrt(c_l) x.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are the training split sequences T, the current SID table (item -> 3 prefixes), and a batch of item latents h in the tangent space at the origin, dimension d=64. Outputs are, every 50 epochs, z*_l and c_l per level; per step, the selected codes k_1,k_2,k_3, the residuals r_l, and the reconstruction/commitment gradients.

specification.text: Quotient and curvature are computed as below; the quantizer is a hyperbolic RQ-VAE whose only curvature input is c_l from the profile target; per level the assignment is argmin_k ||r_l - e_{l,k}|| with r_l the transported Möbius log at p_{l-1}; the prefix step is a geodesic step of the chosen code. Provenance of every constant: m comes from the measured spread, the sign from the L1<L3 evidence, the clip bounds are two standardised units, the codebook occupancy floor is K/2, the recomputation cadence is a cost budget stated as 61 computations over 3000 epochs.

objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

Explore mechanisms in which the TRAINING-ONLY behaviour graph's CURVATURE is computed and used as a design target for the RQ-VAE's prefix geometry, coupled with hyperbolic computation in one connected path, to improve Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065. Evidence to build on (read-only, results/research/sid_generation_forensics/ and analysis_sid_recall/curvature/report.md): over 182 SID tables with their Stage3 recalls, each prefix level's behaviour quotient graph (the training-split co-occurrence graph contracted into the level's prefix groups) has an Ollivier curvature of the lazy random walk; its RAW value is unrelated to the recall (Spearman +0.03, p=0.65) because the level sizes differ, but the STANDARDISED value (real curvature minus a null that keeps the group sizes and shuffles the members, divided by the null's spread) has a level profile: the standardised level-3 curvature correlates POSITIVELY with the recall (+0.26 over all tables, +0.34 over the 115 mechanism families, p=0.001), the standardised level-1 curvature NEGATIVELY (-0.16), and their difference (L1 minus L3) is negative (-0.20, p=0.0095), so a FLATTER curvature profile goes with a better recall; the curvature is not a restatement of the partition's behavioural purity (its rank correlation with the modularity of the same partition is -0.19 to -0.58), but in a joint model the plain SID-quality measures already explain R^2=0.60 of the recall's rank variance and the curvature adds only about one percentage point (level 1 +1.5pp, p=0.017; level 3 +0.8pp, p=0.065; level 2 +0.06pp, p=0.63). The strongest non-geometric predictors are the number of codes the third level actually uses (+0.42) and the collision rate (-0.39). Two open questions for this round: (a) whether the behaviour graph's curvature can be used as a DESIGN TARGET inside the quantizer (a curvature-matching or curvature-profile objective on the prefix embeddings, or a curvature-derived quantity that reweights or reshapes the code assignment) so that the produced SID's quotient graph has a chosen curvature profile, rather than merely predicting which existing SIDs turn out well; (b) whether the standardised profile can enter the LAYER-WISE GEOMETRY of the curved space (per-level curvature, per-level radius or per-level angular budget) in a way that changes the assignment and the gradients. Every proposal must compute its curvature from the TRAINING split only, name the exact quotient graph it measures, couple the curvature to the curved geometry through ONE connected computational path so that removing either the behaviour term or the geometry changes the assignment, and state the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. Note the measured risk this round must address: the Issue #127 arm showed that aligning the codebook to a coarser behavioural partition (a 17-cell hierarchy) made the first level collapse to 4 codes and the recall fall to 0.0513, so a curvature target must not trade resolution away.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
